purpose: Open Company OS control findings. This is audit evidence, not a second delivery backlog; active implementation links to the approved ALM or controlled outage fallback.

findings.finding: No regulated customer or product work package is currently in scope, so a project-specific domain profile cannot be truthfully created in the Company OS.
findings.acceptance: One real project has an approved assurance profile, applicability record, source editions, licence status, market and named human authorities.
findings.alm_reference: Not started until a regulated project is selected
findings.activation_trigger: Before accepting or executing the first regulated, safety-relevant or authority-facing work package, create and approve the domain profile in that external product workspace; absence then becomes an immediate stop.

findings.finding: The declared single-user INTERNAL Company OS path now binds assertions to the Windows logon SID, protects its signing key with current-user DPAPI, restricts runtime ACLs to that principal and SYSTEM, and enforces the processing envelope end to end.
findings.acceptance: A threat-reviewed identity and access path enforces the processing envelope end to end with negative tests and rollback.
findings.closure_evidence: Real Windows-SID/DPAPI/ACL run and synthetic ABAC negatives passed for the exact local INTERNAL scope. Shared, remote, customer or multi-user use remains outside this closure and requires a new activation review.

findings.finding: The declared local store now uses separate blobs, hash-chained history, an HMAC seal, pre-write tamper verification, serialised writes, restricted OS permissions and a verified backup/restore path.
findings.acceptance: Approved storage demonstrates identity, timestamps, hashes, permissions, history, retention, backup and tamper evidence for representative records.
findings.closure_evidence: Real evidence write, ACL observation, HMAC/chain verification and independent-directory restore verification passed. The closure is limited to the founder workstation and does not claim WORM or shared-server storage.

findings.finding: A live local index now retrieves from three controlled Triton policy files admitted by an exact source manifest and returns bounded section-level citations under the access envelope.
findings.acceptance: A bounded index passes held-out retrieval, access, stale-source, poisoning and citation tests without customer-data leakage.
findings.closure_evidence: Real retrieval returned at most five source-path and section citations; exact manifest/source hashes, index integrity, access negatives, stale/poisoned content and cross-tenant leakage checks passed. Customer, licensed-standard and regulated-project corpora are not admitted.

findings.finding: LiteLLM is not installed, pinned, isolated, integrated or approved.
findings.acceptance: A synthetic-data pilot proves scoped keys, approved routes, metadata-only logging, cost/iteration limits, no silent fallback and rollback.

findings.finding: No admitted Presidio service, project-specific IP recognisers or controlled token vault exists.
findings.acceptance: Held-out multilingual and project-identifier tests report false negatives/positives, token-map isolation and output-DLP evidence.

findings.finding: No common qualification/admission evidence exists for simulation, ALM, CAD/BIM, safety or certification-support tools.
findings.acceptance: One representative tool follows a risk-proportionate qualification route with intended use, version, fixtures, limitations, independent review and rollback.

findings.finding: Gateway, RAG, LangGraph, Git, CI, ALM and provider routes lack an end-to-end security and recovery test.
findings.acceptance: A synthetic work package completes the controlled flow and demonstrates failure containment, evidence linkage and recovery.

findings.finding: Local model candidates are not admitted and no suitable vLLM server baseline exists.
findings.acceptance: Exact models and routes pass task-specific quality, latency, resource, privacy, security, cost and rollback gates.

findings.finding: The clean Antigravity Git snapshot at 976b9ee496e4bc6047b97e9e43d1e900e86316db contains 363 tracked files; every file now has SHA-256 identity, authoritative comparison and exactly one reconciled disposition.
findings.acceptance: A frozen source manifest or snapshot diff maps every material changed file group and capability proposal to exactly one disposition ID with count reconciliation.
findings.closure_evidence: test_external_snapshot_manifest.py passed: 363/363 tracked files reconcile to 11/11 disposition groups; source worktree was clean and remained read-only.
